Hi Lee — thanks, appreciate the clarity.

Attached is the subprocessor inventory and our internal redline against your DPA. A couple of notes up front so you have context:

- Subprocessors: attached CSV lists current vendors and regions; most are US/EU-based. We do use a managed KMS provider (US region) for host-level key material. We offer customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private deployments, but not on the standard hosted plan.

- KMS exception: To speed execution, our team is requesting that FinOpsCo accept a limited exception for hosted (non-customer-managed) KMS use. The security tradeoff is documented in the attached security questionnaire.

- Data transfers: We propose standard SCCs + our DPA addendum. If you need an EU-specific addendum, let me know — that will add a couple days to review.

We're aiming to finish signature via DocuSign; I can create the envelope once we align on the KMS language and the subprocessor notification window.

Attaching: redlines-dpa-20260211.docx, subprocessor-inventory-20260211.csv

1) Quick sync if you want to walk through our redlines (15–20m)
2) If you accept the limited KMS exception language, I'll route the DocuSign envelope today
3) If you need stronger controls (customer-managed keys), we'll outline Dedicated/private options and timeline

Thanks —

- Please confirm whether Redwood can accept a 30-day prior notice for subprocessor additions (FinOpsCo requires 30 days, your redline suggests 14).
- Can you confirm that any subprocessor outside the EEA will be subject to SCCs?

FinOpsCo Contracts Team

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: DPA timeline + subprocessors — KMS exception needed (FinOpsCo)

FYI — forwarding FinOpsCo's asks. Need sign-off on the narrow KMS exception and whether we can accept 30-day notice for subprocessors (we usually do 14). Also want an assessment on SCC coverage for non-EEA subprocessors.

Suggested narrow KMS exception language (draft):
"Redwood uses a third-party managed key management service located in the United States for host-level encryption of customer data on our hosted platform. For customers on the hosted plan, Redwood will use such managed KMS for secret management and host-level encryption; for Dedicated and Private deployments Redwood offers the option of customer-managed keys (CMKs). Customer acknowledges and accepts that Redwood's managed KMS may be located in the United States and that Redwood will implement the technical and organizational measures described in Schedule X to protect keys."

Proposed compensating controls to include in Schedule X: encrypted volumes with AES-256, access limited to infra service accounts with 2-person approval for key rotation, and audit logs retained for 12 months.

If Legal (Karthik) and Security (Naomi/Jasmine) can reply with any extra controls or objections, I will send FinOpsCo the updated redline and prepare DocuSign. Procurement wants to know whether the 30-day notice on subprocessors is acceptable from our side.

— Grace

[forwarded attachments: finopsco-dpa-redline-20260211.docx, redlines-dpa-20260211.docx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA timeline + subprocessors — KMS exception needed (FinOpsCo)

Thanks Grace. My read: the narrow exception language is reasonable as long as we harden Schedule X and make the exception explicitly scoped to hosted plan only. A few edits I propose to the draft clause (excerpt):

- Add explicit scoping: "…for the hosted plan (not applicable to Dedicated/Private)"
- Add notice and mitigation: "Redwood will provide written notice of any material change to KMS provider or location and will offer a migration plan for Dedicated/Private customers upon request."
- For subprocessors, we should accept a 30-day notice if we keep a carve-out for emergency onboarding (e.g., security patching) with retro notice within 5 business days in those rare cases.

Naomi/Jasmine: please confirm that Schedule X controls (AES-256, account-level 2-person approvals, 12 months audit logs) meet your bar or if you need increased retention or stricter key custody. If security signs off, I'll incorporate language and push the redline back to FinOpsCo. We can then send the DocuSign envelope — I recommend including the redline as an attachment in the envelope so procurement has the exact agreed text.

— Karthik

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA timeline + subprocessors — KMS exception needed (FinOpsCo)

Karthik / Grace — reviewed. Security will accept the narrow hosted-plan KMS exception with the following additions before we can sign off:

1) Audit log retention extended to 24 months for key access events (we capture only key ops).
2) Mandatory quarterly access reviews for infra service accounts with attestation to the customer upon request.
3) A requirement that any non-EEA subprocessor processing personal data be contractually bound by SCCs; also we need a quick method for FinOpsCo to request a subprocessor data flow diagram for high-risk subprocessors.

Procurement will likely push back on extended retention; if they insist on 12 months we need executive-level risk acceptance. If FinOpsCo is willing to accept 24-month retention for key access logs as a security control, we can finalize the redline and I authorize Grace to send the envelope.

Grace — please update the redline with these items and I'll provide a short sign-off email so you can proceed to DocuSign. Also attach the security questionnaire summary to the envelope; FinOpsCo asked for supporting evidence.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference
